title: Quantum Impurities as Probes of Finite-Temperature Fluctuations in Two-Dimensional Bose Gases
authors: Victor Velasco, Gabriele Spada, Giovanni Midei, Andrea Perali, Luis A. Peña Ardila
abstract: Two-dimensional quantum gases provide a distinctive setting in which enhanced thermal fluctuations, finite-size effects, and two-body bound-state formation are intrinsically intertwined. In this work, we study a single attractive impurity immersed in a finite, weakly interacting two-dimensional Bose gas, where finite size stabilizes a nonzero condensate fraction by introducing an infrared momentum scale, thereby enabling a Bogoliubov description of the bath. Using a hybrid approach that combines finite-temperature many-body scattering theory with input from path-integral Monte Carlo, we analyze the impurity quasiparticle energy across the condensate and normal regimes. The infrared scale generates a phonon-activation temperature below which the impurity energy remains nearly temperature independent. Once the resolved phonon modes become thermally populated, their contribution competes with condensate depletion, producing a nonmonotonic temperature dependence of the polaron energy. These results suggest that attractive Bose polarons may serve as sensitive probes of finite-size thermal fluctuations, phonon dressing, and bound-state physics in low-dimensional Bose gases.
summary: The paper analyzes attractive Bose polarons in 2D Bose gases, using them as spectroscopic tools to measure finite-temperature fluctuations. By combining advanced scattering theory with PIMC simulations, the authors predict a nonmonotonic temperature dependence for the polaron energy due to phonon dressing effects induced by finite size.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum impurities act as sensitive probes for finite-temperature fluctuations, phonon dressing effects, and bound-state physics within two-dimensional Bose gases.
main_result: The impurity quasiparticle energy exhibits a nonmonotonic temperature dependence because the thermal population of resolved phonon modes competes with condensate depletion. This confirms attractive polarons' utility in probing 2D gas dynamics.
method: A hybrid theoretical approach combining finite-temperature many-body scattering theory (e-NSCT) with input from Path-Integral Monte Carlo (PIMC) simulations is employed for analysis.
model_or_system: The system models a single attractive impurity immersed in a weakly interacting, finite two-dimensional Bose gas. The physics incorporates effects arising from the finite size imposing an infrared momentum cutoff ($k_{min}$).
key_observables: Impurity quasiparticle energy, condensate fraction $n_0(T)$, and polaron energy dependence on temperature.
important_parameters: Finite-size effect (IR cutoff $k_{min}$), characteristic temperature $\Theta_c$ (Bogoliubov validity boundary), and the coupling strength ($g$).
main_assumptions: The Bogoliubov description is treated as a low-energy approximation, valid only below the finite-size crossover temperature $\Theta_c$. The analysis relies on treating the system perturbatively in the weak coupling limit.
figures_summary: Figure 1(a) shows the condensate fraction decreasing with T; Figure 1(b) shows correlation functions. Other figures compare polaron splitting results from continuum vs. discrete calculations.
paper_structure: The work builds theory by establishing the Hamiltonian and utilizing Bogoliubov/e-NSCT frameworks, incorporating PIMC results for $n_0(T)$ to analyze the impurity energy across different thermal regimes defined by the finite-size cutoff.
why_interesting: This research directly addresses non-equilibrium dynamics and critical behavior in low-dimensional quantum systems, which is central to modern AMO physics involving ultracold atoms.
